name: Zoth ZeUSD
oneLiner: ZeUSD is Zoth's deprecated V1 RWA-backed dollar token, minted at a fixed collateral valuation and burned to reclaim recorded collateral; V2 is separate.
collateral: U.S. Treasury bills, ETFs, money market funds, and reverse repos (off-chain), and tokenized on-chain RWAs (e.g., Hashnote USYC, Matrixdock STBT, OpenEden TBILL); held in smart contract escrow vaults or traditional/omnibus escrow accounts
pegMechanism: Tracked V1 records collateral value and ZeUSD debt when a deposit is minted, then requires the recorded ZeUSD amount to be burned before returning the recorded collateral. It has no continuing position-health check or forced-liquidation path; the shared deposit/redemption router pause was active at the reviewed finalized block.

oracleRisk.summary: The tracked deprecated V1 uses collateral pricing only when recording a mint. Its verified router later burns the exact recorded ZeUSD debt and returns the recorded collateral, with no ongoing collateral-health oracle or liquidation engine.

branchApplicability.rationale: The tracked V1 router stores collateral value and ZeUSD debt in a deposit NFT at mint, then burns that exact debt and returns the recorded collateral. It exposes no borrower-position repricing, health threshold, or forced-liquidation path. At finalized Ethereum block 25531731 the tracked router proxy still resolved to the reviewed V1 implementation and its shared deposit/redemption pause was active; Zoth's separately deployed V2 is outside this record.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: ZeUSD is issued only on Ethereum as a standard upgradeable ERC20 and bridged via a LayerZero OFT Adapter (lockbox) at 0xBf1060028b212896F799CFbaeA1eD4EEbd060978, which locks canonical ZeUSD on Ethereum (LayerZero Endpoint V2) and mints "ZeUSD OFT" representations on Manta, Metis, and Avalanche. The durable cross-chain supply path is a third-party LayerZero lock/mint Adapter, not an issuer-controlled or DVN-reviewed network.

mintAuthority.summary: ZeUSD token minting is restricted to the V1 router contract; every layer of the control chain (token admin, router admin, router upgrade, AccessController upgrade, and the manta/metis/avalanche OFT representations) resolves to the single Zoth admin EOA 0x3604582f56565d7060d73829ffb9ebd579218dca, verified with no contract bytecode. The router's shared deposit/redemption pause remained active at the reviewed block.

mintIncidents.summary: Zoth's mintWithStable collateral-accounting flaw let an attacker manipulate swap output/LTV validation, mint ZeUSD without sufficient backing, and drain about $285K.
A compromised Zoth admin/deployer key enabled a malicious proxy upgrade of USD0PPSubVaultUpgradeable and drained roughly $8.4M-$8.85M of USD0++ before funds were swapped and moved off-chain.

controls.label: ZeUSD router
controls.evidence: ZeUSD.router() returned this proxy. ZeUSD source shows mint(address,uint256) is onlyRouter; router source exposes mintWithCollateral and mintWithStable routes. Re-verified 2026-07-27 at Ethereum block 25625512: the router's EIP-1967 implementation slot still resolves to the reviewed V1 implementation 0xea25b537209ec4aefbc7252c6a49b132639ea677, accessController() is 0xe81250ed196e45881b78ae92bc978e1de4d61a22, and depositsPaused() is still true.

controls.label: ZeUSD AccessController (router admin and upgrade roles)

sources.label: ZeUSD router implementation (accessController-gated admin and upgrade)

controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25625512 (2026-07-27), this UUPS proxy (implementation 0xf5b1084b3f68f347a6099e3eabb279d9e8be122b) is the router's accessController. getRoleMembers(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE = 0x00) returns exactly one member, the Zoth admin EOA 0x3604582f56565d7060d73829ffb9ebd579218dca; getRoleMembers(UPGRADER_ROLE) likewise returns only that EOA, with roleAdmin = DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE. The verified source gates router admin functions on DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and both the router's and the AccessController's own _authorizeUpgrade on UPGRADER_ROLE, so the whole router administration and upgrade chain terminates at the single EOA.

controls.label: ZeUSD token owner/admin EOA
controls.evidence: ZeUSD.owner() returned this EOA; hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE) and hasRole(ADMIN_ROLE) both returned true. RoleGranted logs show this address received both roles during initialization. Re-verified 2026-07-27 at Ethereum block 25625512: eth_getCode returns empty (plain EOA, no multisig or contract wallet). The same address is owner() of the ZeUSD OFT representations on manta (block 9094790), metis (block 22957771), and avalanche (block 91371517), which are the mint/burn authority for each satellite representation, and it is the sole member of both DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and UPGRADER_ROLE on the router's AccessController.

review.evidence: Control-chain completion review, 2026-07-27: the previously open router-administration and cross-deployment parity questions are resolved on-chain. At Ethereum block 25625512 the router proxy 0x6283F77Db630D6fe69A454ef6cf626e98B117C9b still resolves to the reviewed V1 implementation 0xea25b537209ec4aefbc7252c6a49b132639ea677, accessController() is 0xe81250ed196e45881b78ae92bc978e1de4d61a22 (UUPS, implementation 0xf5b1084b3f68f347a6099e3eabb279d9e8be122b), and depositsPaused() remains true. The AccessController's getRoleMembers returns exactly one member for both DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (0x00) and UPGRADER_ROLE: the Zoth admin EOA 0x3604582f56565d7060d73829ffb9ebd579218dca, whose eth_getCode is empty (no multisig or contract wallet). Verified sources gate router admin functions on DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and the router's, the AccessController's, and the token's upgrade authorizations on UPGRADER_ROLE or token DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, all terminating at the same EOA. Cross-deployment parity verified 2026-07-27: owner() of the ZeUSD OFT representation is the same EOA on manta (block 9094790), metis (block 22957771), and avalanche (block 91371517), and each satellite token is itself an EIP-1967 proxy whose OFT contract is the mint/burn authority for that representation. Every material issuance path therefore concentrates in one externally owned account with no timelock, multisig, or module layer. No public assets-and-liabilities reconciliation or verified prudential-supervision record is published for this token, and the token source carries no supply cap, so economic cap semantics are unbounded.

reserves.issuerOrObligor: Multiple eligible RWA issuers and unspecified escrow counterparties

reserveReview.rationale: Write-time re-open 2026-07-28 of the product page, mechanics page, Terms, and contract-deployments registry (markdown endpoints fetched live): product and Terms still define ZeUSD as RWA-backed against high-quality liquid off-chain/on-chain RWAs including U.S. T-Bills, ETFs, MMFs, and Reverse Repos; mechanics and Terms still state accepted collateral as Treasuries/ETFs/MMFs (on- and off-chain) secured via isolated access-controlled escrow smart-contract vaults (on-chain) and traditional or omnibus escrow accounts (off-chain). The deployments page still labels the tracked Ethereum V1 stack 'Depricated' (token 0x7DC9748DA8E762e569F9269f48F69A1a9F8Ea761, router 0x6283F77Db630D6fe69A454ef6cf626e98B117C9b, historical USYC/wSTBT/T-Bill/wM/USD0++/ZTLN sub-vaults listed without balances) and publishes a separate V2 stack outside this coin's contracts. Independent on-chain corroboration at Ethereum block 25627223: symbol()='ZeUSD', decimals()=6, totalSupply()~27.65M units, and router depositsPaused()=true. No current component allocation, attestation, proof-of-reserves report, or assets-and-liabilities reconciliation is published in any re-opened source, so the single bounded RWA envelope with basket-needs-split and knownUnknownExposurePct=100 is retained; historical sub-vault names are not converted into weights.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Re-opened 2026-07-28: mechanics and Terms still document mixed custody channels — isolated access-controlled escrow smart-contract vaults for on-chain assets and traditional/omnibus escrow for off-chain assets — grounding the mixed segregation rating, but they name no escrow agent, bank, or custodian, publish no account terms, and describe no trust, SPV, or other bankruptcy-remoteness structure, so bankruptcyRemoteness and rehypothecation remain unknown. The Terms still assert a 'fully non-custodial CDP', which holds only for the smart-contract channel; the off-chain escrow channel is custodial by construction and its operator is unidentified. The Terms also give Zoth discretion to liquidate or reinvest collateral into the same RWA product. The tracked V1 stack remains labeled deprecated on the deployments page, and router depositsPaused() was true at Ethereum block 25627223; the March 2025 admin-key compromise that drained roughly $8.4M from a Zoth sub-vault remains direct precedent that access-controlled vault custody can fail. Current collateral inventory, if any, is unreconciled.

notices.title: March 2025 exploit history
notices.message: Zoth suffered March 2025 exploits affecting ZeUSD platform risk, including a collateral-accounting bug and a later admin-key compromise. Review current redemption and reserve evidence before assuming normal peg liquidity. https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-zoth-hack-march-2025

notices.title: Severe residual depeg
notices.message: By late June 2026, ZeUSD market pricing and public liquidity remained far below the $1 peg after the 2025 exploit history, with supply reduced to a small residual base. Treat ZeUSD as a high-risk legacy/depeg case unless current issuer redemption and reserve evidence is independently revalidated.

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: The tracked deprecated V1 is not a continuing borrower CDP: its router fixes collateral value and debt at mint and provides exact burn-and-reclaim redemption without ongoing health checks or forced liquidation. Pharos's closed archetype enum has no exact category for this fixed-mint RWA escrow receipt, so the false CDP label is removed rather than replaced with a materially different fiat issuer or fund-share model.
